name: Losing Loadum
description: Losing Loadum (or Losing Lodam) is an intriguing ancestor of the Hearts family, dating back to 16th-century England. It is a 'penalty trick' game where the objective is to avoid winning specific high-value cards called 'Loaders'. The game is unique for its elimination mechanic: any player reaching 31 points is immediately 'out'. It also features a rare 'hidden trump' system where trumps are determined only when a player first fails to follow suit.

history.origins: First mentioned in 1591. It was a favorite of the Elizabethan and Stuart courts before being simplified into modern Hearts and Black Maria.
timeline: 1590s: Mentioned in 'A Manifest Detection of Dice-Play'.
1670s: Comprehensive rules written by Francis Willughby.
18th Century: Popularity wanes as 'Whist' becomes the dominant trick-taker.
Present: Rediscovered by card historians such as David Parlett.
history.cultural: The name 'Loadum' refers to 'loading' an opponent with unwanted points.
history.evolution: The game's 31-point limit was likely influenced by 'Vingt-Un' (21), but used as a ceiling for loss rather than a goal for victory.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Ranked Ace (high) down to 2.
setup.dealing: Cards are dealt evenly. A small 'talon' of remaining cards is placed face-down.

rules.objective: Avoid reaching 31 points. Point cards: Ace (11), Ten (10), King (3), Queen (2), Jack (1). Total points in deck = 108.
rules.gameplay: 1. Must follow suit. If unable, play any card. 2. **Sudden Trump**: The first time someone cannot follow suit, the top card of the talon is turned over. Its suit becomes trumps for the rest of the round. It is then turned back over, and players must remember it. 3. **Exchanging**: Between tricks, a player can offer 'A coat for a coat' (King/Queen/Jack) or 'A card for a card' (Ace/Ten) to trade high-point cards with opponents, provided the suits match.
keyRules: Point cards: Ace=11, Ten=10, King=3, Queen=2, Jack=1.
Sudden Trump: First time someone cannot follow, talon top card determines trumps (hidden after reveal).
Can exchange high cards between tricks ('coat for coat', 'card for card').

strategy.basic: Keep your 'Loaders' safe. If you have the Ace of Diamonds, lead it early while everyone still has Diamonds. This ensures you 'dump' it without winning a trick filled with other Tens or Aces.
strategy.intermediate: The Trump Memory: Since the trump suit is shown only once and then hidden, many players will forget it. If Spades were shown, lead Spades even if you have only the 2â€”you might catch an opponent 'trumping' with a Diamond because they forgot the rule.
strategy.advanced: The Charge: If you already have 25 points, and you know an opponent is at 28, try to win the next trick with as many point-cards as possible. If you can push them to 31 before you hit it, they lose the life.
tips: Never accept an 'Exchange' offer (Coat/Card) unless you are holding a card of the same suit that you want to dump. It's a risk that usually benefits the proposer.
The 10 is the 'stealth' loader. Most players focus on Aces, but two 10s will put you two-thirds of the way to 31 points.
